note: Textile term ('crespo di Cina'); as adjective 'crespo' = frizzy ('capelli crespi').

ex: Nel ritratto il giovane indossa un farsetto di velluto cremisi allacciato fino al collo.
exEn: In the portrait the young man wears a crimson velvet doublet laced up to the neck.
note: Historical; a padded jacket worn over the shirt from the 14th to the 17th century. Vocabulary of costume and art history.

en: cocked hat; bicorne (academic or diplomatic hat)
ex: Alla cerimonia gli accademici sfilarono con la feluca e il mantello nero.
exEn: At the ceremony the academicians paraded in cocked hats and black cloaks.
note: Also the goliardic hat of university students (pointed, coloured by faculty). Homonym: a small sailing boat (felucca).

ex: Un cappotto frusto e sformato gli pendeva dalle spalle.
exEn: A worn-out, shapeless coat hung from his shoulders.
note: Literary; figurative use is common ('un'espressione frusta' = a hackneyed phrase). Do not confuse with 'frusta' (whip).

ex: Portava pantaloni di fustagno da lavoro e una giacca di velluto a coste.
exEn: He wore work trousers of fustian and a corduroy jacket.
note: Traditional workwear fabric, named after Fustat (Cairo).

ex: Si avvolse nella gabbana e uscì nella tormenta.
exEn: He wrapped himself in his greatcoat and went out into the blizzard.
note: Dated/regional; survives mainly in 'voltagabbana' (turncoat) and 'voltare gabbana'.

ex: Il gentiluomo portava ghette grigie sopra le scarpe lucide, secondo la moda del 1910.
exEn: The gentleman wore grey spats over his polished shoes, as was the fashion in 1910.
note: Almost only plural (singular 'ghetta'). Today used only in mountaineering ('ghette da neve').

ex: La vedova, in gramaglie, seguiva il feretro a capo chino.
exEn: The widow, in mourning dress, followed the coffin with bowed head.
note: Literary, plural only: 'vestire in gramaglie', 'mettersi a gramaglie'. Neutral: 'a lutto'.

ex: L'impuntura a contrasto sui jeans è cucita con filo arancione.
exEn: The contrasting topstitching on the jeans is sewn with orange thread.
note: Tailoring jargon: a seam of close, visible stitches. Verbs: impunturare, impuntire.

en: dressed up to the nines; in one's Sunday best
ex: La domenica le zie si mettevano in ghingheri per la passeggiata sul corso.
exEn: On Sundays the aunts got dressed up to the nines for the stroll along the main street.
note: Familiar/jocular, only in 'mettersi/essere in ghingheri'. Obscure origin (perhaps from 'ghinghero', an old game).

ex: Infagottata in tre maglioni, uscì a spalare la neve.
exEn: Bundled up in three jumpers, she went out to shovel snow.
note: Colloquial/expressive, from 'fagotto' (bundle); implies shapelessness. Cf. 'imbacuccato' (wrapped up warm).

ex: I gomiti lisi della giacca tradivano anni passati alla scrivania.
exEn: The threadbare elbows of his jacket betrayed years spent at a desk.
note: Literary/formal; cf. 'logoro' (worn out, also figurative), 'frusto', 'consunto'.

ex: Teneva le mani nel manicotto di pelliccia, come una dama d'altri tempi.
exEn: She kept her hands in a fur muff, like a lady of bygone days.
note: Also technical: pipe coupling, insulating sleeve. The pasta 'manicotti' is Italian-American.

ex: Le donne entravano in chiesa con la mantiglia di pizzo nero sul capo.
exEn: The women entered the church with black lace mantillas on their heads.
note: From Spanish; Southern and ceremonial usage. Cf. 'velo', 'scialle'.

ex: Il direttore d'orchestra salì sul podio in marsina e cravatta bianca.
exEn: The conductor stepped onto the podium in tails and white tie.
note: From the name of the Comte de Marsin (17th c.). Current synonym: frac. The 'smoking' (tuxedo) is less formal; the 'tight' (morning coat) is daywear.

ex: La modista le provò tre cappellini prima di trovare quello giusto per le corse.
exEn: The milliner tried three little hats on her before finding the right one for the races.
note: Almost always feminine (plural 'modiste'); a man is 'un modista' (plural 'modisti'). Not 'fashion designer' ('stilista').

ex: Un monile d'oro etrusco brillava nella teca del museo.
exEn: An Etruscan gold necklace gleamed in the museum case.
note: Literary/archaeological; everyday 'gioiello', 'collana'.

en: orbace (coarse Sardinian wool cloth, used for Fascist uniforms)
ex: Le divise in orbace erano pesanti e pungenti, ma il regime le impose a tutti.
exEn: The orbace uniforms were heavy and scratchy, but the regime imposed them on everyone.
note: Historical term: coarse Sardinian wool; by antonomasia, the Fascist uniforms of the 1930s.

ex: Si aggirava per casa in una palandrana di lana che gli arrivava alle caviglie.
exEn: He wandered around the house in a loose woollen gown that reached his ankles.
note: Today jocular or pejorative for a loose, shapeless garment. Historical: a dressing gown or long overcoat.

ex: Le tende erano rifinite con una passamaneria dorata da teatro.
exEn: The curtains were finished with a gilt theatrical braid trim.
note: Craft term covering cords, fringes, tassels, galloons; also the shop that sells them.

ex: Il pastrano militare del nonno pesava come una coperta di lana.
exEn: Grandfather's army greatcoat weighed as much as a wool blanket.
note: Dated/literary; 'cappotto' is the neutral word. Cf. 'tabarro' (cloak), 'paltò' (regional).

ex: La sarta riprese le pince del vestito per farlo aderire alla vita.
exEn: The dressmaker took in the darts of the dress to make it fit at the waist.
note: A French loanword of tailoring jargon, invariable; pronounced 'pèns'. 'Pantaloni con le pince' = pleated-front trousers.

ex: Sotto la redingote portava un panciotto di seta a fiori.
exEn: Under his frock coat he wore a flowered silk waistcoat.
note: French loan (from English 'riding coat'), invariable; 19th-century menswear, today a fitted women's coat.

ex: Un mendicante sbrindellato dormiva sotto i portici avvolto in una coperta.
exEn: A beggar in rags was sleeping under the arcades wrapped in a blanket.
note: From 'brindello' (tear, shred). Synonyms: cencioso, stracciato, lacero (literary).

ex: Una giacca sciancrata che segnava la vita e allungava la figura.
exEn: A waisted jacket that defined the waist and lengthened the figure.
note: Tailoring term (from 'anca'); noun 'sciancratura'. Opposite 'diritto', 'a sacco'.

ex: Con i pantaloni sdruciti e le scarpe rotte, sembrava un vagabondo.
exEn: With his ripped trousers and broken shoes, he looked like a tramp.
note: Literary; from 'sdrucire' (to unstitch). Cf. 'sbrindellato', 'cencioso', 'stracciato' (neutral).

ex: Un tempo il prete girava in sottana nera anche per i campi.
exEn: Once upon a time the priest went about in a black cassock even through the fields.
note: Dated for 'gonna'; today used for the priest's cassock. Pejorative: 'attaccato alle sottane della madre' (tied to his mother's apron strings).

ex: Una giacca di tweed spigato, con le toppe ai gomiti.
exEn: A herringbone tweed jacket with elbow patches.
note: Tailoring; also noun 'lo spigato'. Everyday equivalent 'a spina di pesce'.

ex: Con il ritorno della moda anni Cinquanta, lo spolverino di seta è di nuovo nelle vetrine.
exEn: With the return of Fifties fashion, the silk duster coat is back in shop windows.
note: A light overcoat worn to keep off dust (open cars, trains). Also: a dusting tool.

en: train (of a dress); aftermath, lingering consequence
ex: Due paggi reggevano lo strascico dell'abito nuziale lungo la navata.
exEn: Two page-boys carried the train of the wedding dress down the nave.
note: Figurative sense is very common: 'la vicenda ha lasciato strascichi giudiziari'. Also 'pesca a strascico' (trawling).

ex: Avvolto nel tabarro, il contadino attraversò la piazza nella nebbia.
exEn: Wrapped in his heavy cloak, the farmer crossed the square in the fog.
note: Historical/regional (Veneto, Emilia); 'Il tabarro' is an opera by Puccini. The diminutive 'tabarrino' has come back into fashion.

ex: Il parroco indossava ancora la veste talare, come cinquant'anni fa.
exEn: The parish priest still wore the cassock, just as fifty years ago.
note: From Latin 'talus' (heel); almost only in 'veste/abito talare'. Cf. 'tonaca', 'saio' (friars).

ex: Lo sposo indossava un tight grigio perla con il cilindro.
exEn: The groom wore a pearl-grey morning suit with a top hat.
note: False friend: in Italian 'tight' is the morning coat, never tights ('collant'). Invariable, pronounced 'tait'.

ex: Il gondoliere in costume settecentesco portava un tricorno nero.
exEn: The gondolier in eighteenth-century costume wore a black tricorn.
note: Historical; associated with Goldoni's Venice and the carabinieri's dress uniform ('la lucerna').

ex: Nella Bohème il filosofo Colline canta l'addio alla sua vecchia zimarra.
exEn: In La Bohème the philosopher Colline sings a farewell to his old overcoat.
note: Dated/literary; historically a loose gown for men and clergy. Cf. 'palandrana'.

en: hooked; aquiline (of a nose, beak, claw)
ex: Il rapace serrava la preda negli artigli adunchi.
exEn: The raptor gripped its prey in its hooked talons.
note: Literary Latinism (aduncus); 'naso adunco'. Cf. 'uncinato' (hook-shaped, technical), 'aquilino' (of noses only).

ex: Una luce argentea filtrava tra le nuvole sul mare.
exEn: A silvery light filtered through the clouds over the sea.
note: Literary; distinguish from 'argentato' (silver-plated) and 'argentino' (silvery in sound).

ex: Nella stagione aurea del Rinascimento Firenze dettava il gusto all'Europa.
exEn: In the golden age of the Renaissance, Florence dictated taste to Europe.
note: Literary; 'sezione aurea' (golden ratio), 'aurea mediocritas'. Literal 'gold-coloured' is 'dorato'.

ex: Un cielo bigio prometteva pioggia per tutto il giorno.
exEn: A drab grey sky promised rain for the whole day.
note: Tuscan/literary; 'né bianco né bigio' = neither one thing nor the other. Cf. 'grigio' (neutral), 'cinereo', 'plumbeo'.

ex: Il disegno è eseguito a penna e bistro su carta avorio.
exEn: The drawing is executed in pen and bistre on ivory paper.
note: Art term; also invariable adjective ('bruno bistro'). Not the French café, which in Italian is 'bistrot'.

ex: L'acciaio brunito della canna non rifletteva la luce.
exEn: The burnished steel of the barrel did not reflect the light.
note: Technical (gunsmithing, goldsmithing: 'brunitura'); literary for dark gleaming surfaces.

ex: Un vecchio canuto sedeva ogni mattina sulla panchina davanti alla chiesa.
exEn: A white-haired old man sat every morning on the bench in front of the church.
note: Literary; noun 'canizie' (white hair, old age). Neutral: 'con i capelli bianchi'; 'brizzolato' = greying.

ex: Le labbra dipinte di carminio spiccavano sul viso pallidissimo.
exEn: Her carmine-painted lips stood out against her very pale face.
note: Art and cosmetics; also invariable adjective ('rosso carminio'). Historically extracted from cochineal.

ex: Lo sguardo ceruleo del bambino sembrava riflettere il cielo.
exEn: The child's cerulean gaze seemed to reflect the sky.
note: Literary; also a pigment ('blu ceruleo'). Cf. 'azzurro' (neutral), 'cilestrino', 'turchino'.

ex: Le mura ciclopiche di Alatri sono fatte di blocchi incastrati senza malta.
exEn: The cyclopean walls of Alatri are made of blocks fitted together without mortar.
note: Archaeological term for huge polygonal masonry; figuratively 'uno sforzo ciclopico'. Cf. 'immane', 'mastodontico'.

ex: Un velo cilestrino avvolgeva le montagne lontane.
exEn: A pale-blue veil enveloped the distant mountains.
note: Literary diminutive of 'cilestro/celeste'; Tuscan flavour. Cf. 'celeste' (neutral), 'ceruleo' (deeper, poetic).

ex: Il cielo cinereo di novembre pesava sulla città.
exEn: November's ashen sky weighed on the city.
note: From 'cenere'; literary, often of complexions and skies. Cf. 'cenerino' (neutral grey), 'grigio cenere'.

ex: Il sipario cremisi del teatro si alzò tra gli applausi.
exEn: The theatre's crimson curtain rose amid applause.
note: Invariable adjective and noun (from Arabic qirmiz, the kermes insect). Cf. 'scarlatto', 'vermiglio', 'porpora'.

ex: Le tavolette d'argilla recavano iscrizioni cuneiformi.
exEn: The clay tablets bore cuneiform inscriptions.
note: Learned (Latin 'cuneus', wedge); also anatomical ('ossa cuneiformi').

ex: Aveva capelli d'ebano e una pelle chiarissima, come nella fiaba.
exEn: She had ebony hair and very pale skin, as in the fairy tale.
note: The wood and, in comparisons, the colour: 'nero come l'ebano', 'capelli d'ebano'. 'Ebanista' = cabinet-maker.

ex: Il collo eburneo della statua contrasta con il bronzo scuro del piedistallo.
exEn: The statue's ivory neck contrasts with the dark bronze of the pedestal.
note: Literary (from Latin ebur, ivory: 'avorio'). 'Torre eburnea' = ivory tower (also 'torre d'avorio').

ex: Ha scelto tende di lino ecrù per la camera degli ospiti.
exEn: She chose ecru linen curtains for the guest room.
note: Invariable; textile term from French 'écru'. Also spelt 'écru'.

ex: Un cielo ferrigno pesava sulla pianura gelata.
exEn: An iron-grey sky weighed on the frozen plain.
note: Literary; also of character or bodies ('una tempra ferrigna').

ex: I muri fuligginosi della vecchia stazione raccontavano un secolo di locomotive a vapore.
exEn: The sooty walls of the old station told of a century of steam locomotives.
note: Literary; from 'fuliggine' (soot). Cf. 'nerastro', 'cinereo'.

ex: Le foglie fusiformi dell'oleandro resistono bene alla siccità.
exEn: The spindle-shaped leaves of the oleander withstand drought well.
note: Botanical/anatomical; from 'fuso' (spindle). Cf. 'affusolato' (tapered, of fingers).

ex: Portava una collana di giaietto, nera e lucente come i suoi capelli.
exEn: She wore a necklace of jet, black and shining like her hair.
note: Literary/jewellery term; 'nero come il giaietto'. Cf. 'ebano' (ebony), 'corvino' (raven-black), 'pece' (pitch).

ex: La luna gibbosa illuminava il sentiero quanto bastava per non cadere.
exEn: The gibbous moon lit the path just enough to keep us from falling.
note: Learned/astronomical ('luna gibbosa' between half and full); of terrain, 'un terreno gibboso'. Noun 'gibbosità'. Everyday 'gobbo'.

ex: I suoi occhi glauchi avevano il colore del mare d'inverno.
exEn: Her sea-green eyes had the colour of the winter sea.
note: Poetic Greek-derived colour (D'Annunzio loved it); medical 'glaucoma' is related. Plural 'glauchi/glauche' keeps the hard c.

ex: I tifosi granata invasero la piazza dopo il derby.
exEn: The garnet-red (Torino) fans flooded the square after the derby.
note: Invariable; 'granata' is the emblematic colour of Torino FC. Homonyms: pomegranate, hand grenade.

ex: Il pittore rese l'incarnato della modella con sottili velature rosate.
exEn: The painter rendered the model's flesh tones with subtle pinkish glazes.
note: Art-historical and literary; 'incarnato di pesca'. As adjective: 'rosa incarnato'.

ex: Una nube lenticolare, immobile sopra la vetta, annunciava vento in quota.
exEn: A lenticular cloud, motionless above the summit, announced wind at altitude.
note: Technical (meteorology, optics, galaxies); from 'lenticchia'.

ex: Serviva le portate su piattini lillipuziani, con porzioni da nouvelle cuisine.
exEn: She served the courses on Lilliputian little plates, with nouvelle-cuisine portions.
note: Learned/jocular, from Swift's Lilliput; opposite 'gargantuesco', 'ciclopico'.

ex: Un lucore verdastro filtrava dalle persiane socchiuse.
exEn: A faint greenish glow filtered through the half-closed shutters.
note: Literary; weaker than 'chiarore' and 'bagliore', stronger than 'barlume'. From Latin 'lucor'.

ex: Il taglio di manzo era ben marezzato, con sottili venature di grasso.
exEn: The cut of beef was well marbled, with fine veins of fat.
note: From 'marezzo' (marble-like veining); of wood, silk, paper and meat. 'Marezzatura' is now a gastronomy word.

ex: Un niveo candore avvolgeva la valle dopo la nevicata.
exEn: A snowy whiteness enveloped the valley after the snowfall.
note: Poetic Latinism (nix, nivis); 'nivea pelle', 'niveo mantello'. Cf. 'candido', 'eburneo'.

ex: L'alba lasciò sul mare una luce opalescente, tra il rosa e il grigio.
exEn: Dawn left an opalescent light on the sea, between pink and grey.
note: From 'opale'; literary and technical (vetro opalescente). Cf. 'iridescente', 'lattiginoso', 'perlaceo'.

ex: Ha dipinto la parete del soggiorno di un ottanio profondo.
exEn: She painted the living-room wall a deep teal.
note: Invariable; fashion and interior-design term ('blu ottanio', 'verde ottanio'). Near-synonym 'petrolio'.

ex: La testa ovoidale delle figure di Modigliani è inconfondibile.
exEn: The egg-shaped heads of Modigliani's figures are unmistakable.
note: Technical/art term for three-dimensional shapes; 'ovale' is the flat figure.

ex: Il vino ha un colore giallo paglierino con riflessi verdolini.
exEn: The wine is straw-yellow in colour with greenish glints.
note: Wine-tasting cliché ('giallo paglierino'); from 'paglia'. Cf. 'dorato' (golden), 'ambrato' (amber).

ex: Divenne paonazzo dalla rabbia e uscì sbattendo la porta.
exEn: He turned purple with rage and went out slamming the door.
note: From 'pavone' (peacock). Used almost only of faces: 'paonazzo per il freddo/la rabbia/lo sforzo'. Also 'pavonazzo' (older).

ex: Indossava un abito pervinca che le illuminava gli occhi.
exEn: She wore a periwinkle-blue dress that lit up her eyes.
note: Invariable colour adjective ('blu pervinca'); as feminine noun it is the plant.

ex: Una mucca pezzata pascolava vicino al torrente.
exEn: A piebald cow was grazing near the stream.
note: Zootechnical ('pezzata rossa' is a cattle breed); 'pezzatura' = pattern of patches. Cf. 'maculato', 'screziato'.

ex: Le vetrate policrome inondano la navata di luce colorata.
exEn: The polychrome stained-glass windows flood the nave with coloured light.
note: Art-historical; stress 'polìcromo'. Opposite 'monocromo'. Noun 'policromia'.

ex: Un tramonto porporino incendiava il cielo sopra la laguna.
exEn: A crimson-purple sunset set the sky over the lagoon ablaze.
note: Literary; 'porpora' is the noun (also the cardinal's rank). Cf. 'purpureo' (more solemn), 'cremisi'.

ex: Il tramonto tingeva di purpuree striature le nubi sull'orizzonte.
exEn: The sunset streaked the clouds on the horizon with crimson.
note: Poetic; from 'porpora', the ancient imperial dye (red-violet, not English purple). Cf. 'porporino'.

ex: I riflessi ramati dei suoi capelli si accendevano al sole.
exEn: The coppery highlights in her hair lit up in the sun.
note: From 'rame' (copper); also literally 'coated with copper' (pentola ramata, vite ramate = copper-sprayed vines).

ex: Il quadro era appeso a sghimbescio e nessuno se ne accorgeva.
exEn: The picture hung askew and nobody noticed.
note: Colloquial-literary, almost always in 'a sghimbescio' or 'di sghimbescio'; synonyms 'di sbieco', 'di traverso', 'storto' (neutral).

ex: Aveva il volto terreo di chi non dorme da giorni.
exEn: He had the ashen face of someone who has not slept for days.
note: From 'terra'; used almost only of faces ('colorito terreo'). Cf. 'cinereo', 'cereo' (waxen), 'smorto'.

ex: La Fata Turchina, nelle Avventure di Pinocchio, ha i capelli di questo colore.
exEn: The Blue Fairy in Pinocchio has hair of this colour.
note: Between 'azzurro' and 'blu'; literary and fairy-tale flavour (from 'turco', via Turkish blue dye). Cf. 'turchese' (turquoise).

ex: Le statue di bronzo del giardino erano coperte di verderame.
exEn: The bronze statues in the garden were covered in verdigris.
note: Also the copper-based fungicide sprayed on vines; adjective use 'verde verderame'.

ex: Portava una sciarpa vinaccia su un cappotto grigio ferro.
exEn: He wore a dark wine-red scarf over an iron-grey coat.
note: Invariable as colour ('color vinaccia'); as feminine noun 'le vinacce' are the pressed grape skins distilled into grappa.

ex: Vi scrivo acciocché sappiate la verità prima che altri ve la raccontino a modo loro.
exEn: I am writing to you so that you may know the truth before others tell it their own way.
note: Archaic/literary, takes the subjunctive; modern 'affinché'.

ex: Non ho alcunché da aggiungere a quanto ho già dichiarato.
exEn: I have nothing whatsoever to add to what I have already stated.
note: Formal; typical of legal and official statements.

ex: Stava per uscire allorché squillò il telefono.
exEn: He was about to go out when the telephone rang.
note: Formal/literary; also legal ('allorché ricorrano i presupposti').

ex: Il contratto si risolve allorquando una delle parti non adempia alle proprie obbligazioni.
exEn: The contract is terminated when one of the parties fails to fulfil its obligations.
note: Bureaucratic-literary; heavier than 'allorché'.

ex: «Avvegnaché io sia vecchio, non ho perduto la memoria», scriveva il cronista.
exEn: 'Although I am old, I have not lost my memory,' wrote the chronicler.
note: Archaic, found in Dante and Boccaccio; today only jocular or in pastiche. Takes the subjunctive.

ex: Checché se ne dica, la riforma ha prodotto qualche risultato.
exEn: Whatever people may say, the reform has produced some results.
note: Fixed in 'checché se ne dica', 'checché ne pensi'; always with subjunctive.

ex: Le prove erano scarse; cionondimeno la giuria lo condannò.
exEn: The evidence was thin; nevertheless the jury convicted him.
note: Formal/bureaucratic; also 'ciononostante', 'nondimeno'. Neutral 'tuttavia', 'comunque'.

ex: Comecché fosse povero, non chiese mai nulla a nessuno.
exEn: Although he was poor, he never asked anyone for anything.
note: Archaic/literary; takes the subjunctive.

ex: Non insistette, conciossiaché sapesse di avere torto.
exEn: He did not insist, since he knew he was in the wrong.
note: Archaic; the very type of pompous old-fashioned connector, cited ironically. Variant 'conciossiacosaché'.

ex: Dacché è andato in pensione non ha più aperto un giornale.
exEn: Since he retired he has not opened a newspaper.
note: Literary; 'dacché mondo è mondo' = since the world began.

en: a little while ago; just before
ex: Come dicevo dianzi, la questione merita un esame più attento.
exEn: As I was saying a little while ago, the matter deserves closer examination.
note: Literary; synonyms 'poc'anzi', 'testé'.

ex: Tornò al paese donde era partito trent'anni prima.
exEn: He returned to the village whence he had set out thirty years before.
note: Literary; also 'onde'. Modern 'da dove'.

ex: «E ciò dico eziandio per coloro che non vollero ascoltare», conclude l'orazione.
exEn: 'And this I say also for those who would not listen,' the oration concludes.
note: Archaic; cited as a byword for antiquated language. Only in parody or historical texts.

ex: Il senatore pronunciò una filippica di un'ora contro la riforma.
exEn: The senator delivered an hour-long philippic against the reform.
note: Learned (Demosthenes against Philip of Macedon, then Cicero); near-synonyms 'invettiva' (invective), 'diatriba', colloquial 'tirata', 'sfuriata'.

ex: Ha rinunciato a tutto, financo al nome di famiglia.
exEn: He gave up everything, even the family name.
note: Literary; variant 'finanche'. Modern 'perfino', 'persino'.

ex: Giammai avrei immaginato di rivederlo in quelle circostanze.
exEn: Never would I have imagined seeing him again in those circumstances.
note: Literary/emphatic; in speech often jocular ('Giammai!').

ex: Non temere, imperocché nulla ti sarà chiesto che tu non possa dare.
exEn: Fear not, for nothing will be asked of you that you cannot give.
note: Archaic/literary; now used only for solemn or parodic effect.

ex: Si fermò un istante sulla soglia, indi entrò senza bussare.
exEn: He paused an instant on the threshold, then went in without knocking.
note: Literary; also in 'indi per cui' (jocular pompous 'therefore').

ex: Le prove erano insufficienti, laonde l'imputato fu assolto.
exEn: The evidence was insufficient, wherefore the accused was acquitted.
note: Archaic; from 'là onde'. Today ironic or in historical prose.

ex: La notizia lo rese oltremodo felice.
exEn: The news made him exceedingly happy.
note: Literary intensifier; also 'oltre modo'.

ex: La sentenza è stata pubblicata con numerosi omissis a tutela dei minori coinvolti.
exEn: The judgment was published with numerous redactions to protect the minors involved.
note: Legal/journalistic Latinism, invariable; written '(omissis)' where text is left out. Verb phrase 'omissare' is jargon.

ex: Le due proposte sono parimenti inaccettabili.
exEn: The two proposals are equally unacceptable.
note: Formal; also 'parimente'.

ex: «Salire su» e «uscire fuori» sono perissologie che la lingua parlata tollera.
exEn: 'Salire su' and 'uscire fuori' are redundancies that spoken language tolerates.
note: Rhetoric/linguistics; near-synonyms 'pleonasmo' (the usual term), 'ridondanza'. 'Tautologia' repeats the idea, 'perissologia' adds superfluous words.

ex: Non si diede per vinto, perocché la speranza era l'unica cosa che gli restava.
exEn: He did not give up, for hope was the only thing he had left.
note: Archaic; Dante uses 'però che'. Only literary or parodic today.

ex: «Poscia, più che 'l dolor, poté 'l digiuno», dice Ugolino.
exEn: 'Then, more than grief, hunger prevailed,' says Ugolino.
note: Archaic, Dantesque; today only in quotation or parody.

ex: Sapeva di avere poche possibilità; purtuttavia decise di candidarsi.
exEn: He knew he had little chance; nevertheless he decided to stand.
note: Formal; a reinforced 'tuttavia'.

ex: Il vescovo rivolse una severa rampogna ai fedeli che disertavano la messa.
exEn: The bishop addressed a stern rebuke to the faithful who were skipping Mass.
note: Literary; verb 'rampognare'. Scale of reproofs: 'rimprovero' (neutral), 'rimbrotto', 'rampogna', 'reprimenda' (formal), 'ramanzina' (colloquial).

ex: Tornò a casa tardi e si prese i soliti rimbrotti della madre.
exEn: He came home late and got the usual scolding from his mother.
note: Literary-colloquial; verb 'rimbrottare'. Milder and more domestic than 'rampogna'; cf. 'brontolio' (grumbling).

en: with him; with her; with himself (archaic)
ex: Portò seco il figlio minore e lasciò gli altri alla balia.
exEn: He took his youngest son with him and left the others with the wet-nurse.
note: Archaic/literary (Latin secum); the series 'meco, teco, seco'. In modern Italian only 'con sé', 'con lui'. Still heard in 'recare seco'.

ex: Tutto sembrava risolto; sennonché il giorno dopo arrivò una nuova denuncia.
exEn: Everything seemed settled; but then the next day a new complaint arrived.
note: Literary-formal; introduces an unexpected obstacle. Also spelled 'se non che'.

ex: In siffatte circostanze, ogni ulteriore trattativa sarebbe inutile.
exEn: In such circumstances, any further negotiation would be pointless.
note: Formal/literary (sì + fatto); neutral 'simile', 'tale', 'del genere'. Legal prose still uses it.

ex: Sovente i grandi cambiamenti nascono da eventi apparentemente insignificanti.
exEn: Often great changes arise from apparently insignificant events.
note: Literary; also regional (Piedmont) in ordinary speech. Modern 'spesso'.

en: so that; with the result that
ex: La pioggia cadde per giorni, talché il fiume straripò.
exEn: The rain fell for days, so that the river overflowed.
note: Literary; also 'sì che', 'cosicché'.

ex: Come ho testé ricordato, il problema non è nuovo.
exEn: As I recalled a moment ago, the problem is not new.
note: Formal/literary; also spelled 'testè'. Synonyms 'poc'anzi', 'or ora'.

ex: Non aveva veruna intenzione di restituire il denaro.
exEn: He had no intention whatsoever of returning the money.
note: Archaic/bureaucratic; used only in negative or interrogative sentences, like 'alcuno'. Forms: veruno, veruna. Manzoni uses it freely.

en: more and more; all the more
ex: La situazione si faceva vieppiù confusa a ogni nuova dichiarazione.
exEn: The situation grew ever more confused with each new statement.
note: Literary; also spelled 'viepiù'. Modern 'sempre più'.

ex: Dopo la carbonara mi è venuto un abbiocco tremendo e ho dormito un'ora.
exEn: After the carbonara I was hit by a terrible drowsiness and slept for an hour.
note: Colloquial, originally Roman, now nationwide; 'avere/venire l'abbiocco', verb 'abbioccarsi'. Neutral 'sonnolenza'.

ex: Terminate le abluzioni mattutine, scese a fare colazione in vestaglia.
exEn: His morning ablutions over, he came down to breakfast in his dressing gown.
note: Literally a ritual washing (Islam, Judaism); in everyday use jocular for washing oneself. Mostly plural.

ex: La trovai affaccendata tra i fornelli, con tre pentole sul fuoco.
exEn: I found her bustling about at the stove, with three pots on the go.
note: Literary-colloquial; from 'faccenda'. Cf. 'indaffarato' (neutral), 'occupato' (plain).

ex: Ha comprato un aggeggio che dovrebbe sbucciare le mele da solo.
exEn: He bought a contraption that is supposed to peel apples by itself.
note: Colloquial, slightly dismissive; near-synonyms 'marchingegno' (complicated device), 'arnese' (tool), 'coso' (thingummy).

ex: Le operaie lavoravano alacri per finire la commessa prima di Natale.
exEn: The women worked briskly to finish the order before Christmas.
note: Literary; noun 'alacrità', adverb 'alacremente'. Latinism (alacer); stress on the first syllable: àlacre.

ex: La scrivania era ingombra di ammennicoli: fermacarte, penne rotte, foto sbiadite.
exEn: The desk was cluttered with odds and ends: paperweights, broken pens, faded photos.
note: Literary/jocular; also 'quibble, pretext' in old legal language. Synonyms: aggeggio, ninnolo, orpello.

ex: Per lui centomila euro erano una bagattella.
exEn: For him a hundred thousand euros were a trifle.
note: Often ironic for a sum that is actually large. In music: a short composition (Beethoven's Bagatelles).

ex: Litigarono per una bazzecola e non si parlarono per un anno.
exEn: They quarrelled over a trifle and did not speak for a year.
note: Familiar, often ironic ('costa una bazzecola: diecimila euro'). Synonyms: inezia, quisquilia, sciocchezza, bagattella.

en: odds and ends; bits and pieces; belongings
ex: Raccolse le sue carabattole in una valigia e se ne andò senza salutare.
exEn: He gathered his bits and pieces into a suitcase and left without saying goodbye.
note: Plural only, familiar/jocular. Synonyms: cianfrusaglie, masserizie (more serious), bagagli.

ex: Svuotando la soffitta trovammo scatoloni pieni di cianfrusaglie che nessuno voleva buttare.
exEn: Emptying the attic we found boxes full of junk that nobody wanted to throw away.
note: Familiar, usually plural. Synonyms: ciarpame (more pejorative), carabattole, paccottiglia (shoddy goods).

ex: Il garage era diventato un deposito di ciarpame che nessuno aveva il coraggio di smaltire.
exEn: The garage had become a dump of junk that nobody had the courage to get rid of.
note: Collective, pejorative (suffix -ame). Figurative: 'ciarpame ideologico'. Synonym: robaccia.

ex: Solo una fatica diuturna gli permise di finire l'opera in dieci anni.
exEn: Only unremitting daily toil allowed him to finish the work in ten years.
note: Elevated (aulico; Latin diuturnus). Not to be confused with 'diurno' (of the day): 'diuturno' combines the ideas of long duration and daily recurrence.

ex: Passa le ore a smontare e rimontare i suoi gingilli elettronici.
exEn: He spends hours taking apart and reassembling his electronic toys.
note: Familiar, often jocular for a tech gadget. Verb: gingillarsi (to dawdle, waste time).

ex: Senza indugio prese il cappotto e uscì sotto la pioggia.
exEn: Without delay he grabbed his coat and went out into the rain.
note: Formal/literary. Idioms: 'senza indugio', 'rompere gli indugi' (to make up one's mind). Verb: indugiare.

ex: I lavori stradali sono un intralcio continuo alla circolazione del quartiere.
exEn: The roadworks are a constant hindrance to traffic in the neighbourhood.
note: Formal; 'essere d'intralcio a', 'intralcio alla giustizia' (obstruction of justice, legal). Cf. 'intoppo' (snag), 'impiccio' (nuisance).

ex: Lesto come un gatto, afferrò il vassoio prima che cadesse.
exEn: Quick as a cat, he grabbed the tray before it fell.
note: Familiar/literary. 'Lesto di mano' = light-fingered, a thief; 'lesto di lingua' = quick with a reply. Synonyms: svelto, agile, spedito.

ex: La cucina era linda e profumava di limone.
exEn: The kitchen was spotless and smelt of lemon.
note: Literary-colloquial, often in 'lindo e pinto' (neat as a pin). Neutral 'pulito'; 'terso' is used of air, sky and glass.

ex: Aveva costruito un marchingegno di corde e carrucole per aprire la finestra dal letto.
exEn: He had built a contraption of ropes and pulleys to open the window from his bed.
note: Jocular; also figurative: 'un marchingegno fiscale' (a tax dodge). Synonyms: aggeggio, congegno (neutral), trabiccolo.

ex: Caricarono le masserizie su un carro e lasciarono il paese per sempre.
exEn: They loaded their household goods onto a cart and left the village for good.
note: Almost only plural; literary or bureaucratic in tone (inventories, house moves). From 'massaro' (steward of an estate).

en: small fry; odds and ends; trivial details
ex: Il cassetto era pieno di minutaglia: bottoni, chiavi, tappi e ricevute.
exEn: The drawer was full of odds and ends: buttons, keys, corks and receipts.
note: Colloquial-literary, slightly dismissive; also of small fish or unimportant people. Cf. 'minuzia' (a trifle), 'cianfrusaglie'.

ex: Le mensole erano piene di ninnoli di porcellana comprati nei viaggi.
exEn: The shelves were full of porcelain knick-knacks bought on trips.
note: A small decorative object of no value. Synonyms: soprammobile (neutral), gingillo, chincaglieria.

ex: I nottambuli del centro si ritrovano al chiosco del cornetto caldo alle quattro del mattino.
exEn: The city-centre night owls meet at the hot-croissant kiosk at four in the morning.
note: Also adjective; formed on the model of 'sonnambulo' (sleepwalker). Opposite 'mattiniero' (early riser).

ex: Dopo pranzo, d'estate, a Roma è sacra la pennichella.
exEn: After lunch, in summer, the afternoon nap is sacred in Rome.
note: Roman regional, now widespread everywhere with a jocular tone. Synonyms: pisolino, sonnellino, siesta; 'schiacciare un pisolino'.

ex: La sua pignoleria nel controllare ogni scontrino esasperava i colleghi.
exEn: His fussiness in checking every receipt exasperated his colleagues.
note: Colloquial, mildly pejorative; from 'pignolo'. Positive equivalents 'meticolosità', 'scrupolo'; near-synonym 'pedanteria' (of scholars).

ex: Non disturbare il direttore per simili quisquilie.
exEn: Do not bother the director with such petty matters.
note: A Latinism, often ironic; made famous by Totò ('quisquilie e pinzillacchere'). Almost always plural.

ex: Le calze di lana avevano rammendi su rammendi, ma erano ancora calde.
exEn: The woollen socks had darning upon darning, but they were still warm.
note: A household chore of bygone days; the 'uovo da rammendo' was the wooden darning egg. Verb: rammendare. Compare 'rattoppo' (with a patch).

ex: Il tetto reggeva grazie a una serie di rattoppi che ogni inverno diventavano più precari.
exEn: The roof held up thanks to a series of patches that grew more precarious every winter.
note: Concrete (a patch on fabric) and figurative (a stopgap: 'politica dei rattoppi'). Verb: rattoppare.

ex: La sciatteria della traduzione rendeva il libro quasi illeggibile.
exEn: The sloppiness of the translation made the book almost unreadable.
note: From 'sciatto'; applies to people, work and style. Synonyms: trascuratezza, negligenza, trasandatezza.

ex: Lasciare le luci accese tutto il giorno è uno sciupio inutile.
exEn: Leaving the lights on all day is a pointless waste.
note: Familiar/Tuscan, from 'sciupare'. Synonyms: spreco (common), sperpero (of money), dissipazione.

ex: Un gruppo di giovani sfaccendati passava le giornate sulla panchina della piazza.
exEn: A group of idle youths spent their days on the bench in the square.
note: Mildly pejorative, also a noun ('uno sfaccendato'). Register between 'disoccupato' (neutral) and 'fannullone', 'scioperato' (harsher).

ex: Un impiegato solerte aveva già preparato tutte le pratiche prima del nostro arrivo.
exEn: A diligent clerk had already prepared all the paperwork before we arrived.
note: Formal, sometimes ironic ('i solerti vigili'). Noun: solerzia. Synonyms: zelante, sollecito, operoso.

ex: Per sollazzo dei cortigiani si organizzavano cacce, giostre e balli mascherati.
exEn: For the courtiers' amusement, hunts, jousts and masked balls were organised.
note: Literary/archaic, today jocular ('a sollazzo del pubblico'). Verb: sollazzarsi. Synonyms: svago, diletto, spasso.

ex: Il caldo del pomeriggio immerse la casa in un sopore dal quale nessuno voleva uscire.
exEn: The afternoon heat plunged the house into a drowsiness no one wanted to leave.
note: Literary/medical ('stato soporoso'); Latinism (sopor). Everyday 'sonnolenza', figurative 'torpore'.

ex: Sotto il frigorifero c'era un sudiciume di anni.
exEn: Under the fridge there was years' worth of grime.
note: Pejorative; adjective 'sudicio'. Stronger than 'sporcizia'; 'luridume', 'lordura' are literary equivalents.

ex: La casa fu venduta con tutte le suppellettili, dai lampadari alle posate.
exEn: The house was sold with all its furnishings, from the chandeliers to the cutlery.
note: Formal/bureaucratic, mostly plural. In archaeology: 'suppellettile funeraria' (grave goods).

en: prevarication; beating about the bush; evasiveness
ex: Dopo settimane di tergiversazioni, la direzione diede finalmente una risposta.
exEn: After weeks of prevarication, the management finally gave an answer.
note: Formal; from 'tergiversare' (Latin tergum vertere, to turn one's back). False friend: not English 'tergiversation' in the sense of apostasy.

ex: Dopo il temporale il cielo era terso e si vedevano le Alpi.
exEn: After the storm the sky was clear and you could see the Alps.
note: Literary; of sky, air, glass and, figuratively, of prose style ('una prosa tersa'). From 'tergere' (to wipe).

ex: I cavi dietro la televisione formavano un viluppo inestricabile.
exEn: The cables behind the television formed an inextricable tangle.
note: Literary; figurative: 'un viluppo di sentimenti/interessi'. Synonyms: groviglio (common), garbuglio, intrico.

ex: La luce abbacinante del mezzogiorno cancellava ogni ombra dalla piazza.
exEn: The dazzling midday light erased every shadow from the square.
note: Literary; from 'bacino' (the basin of red-hot metal once used to blind prisoners). Figurative: 'una bellezza abbacinante'.

en: unripe; sour; immature; (fig.) bitter, premature, harsh
ex: Un dolore acerbo la colse alla notizia della morte acerba del fratello.
exEn: A bitter grief seized her at the news of her brother's untimely death.
note: Literary senses beyond 'unripe': 'morte acerba' (early death), 'critiche acerbe' (harsh), 'talento acerbo' (immature).

ex: Una paura atavica del buio lo accompagnava fin dall'infanzia.
exEn: An atavistic fear of the dark had accompanied him since childhood.
note: From Latin 'atavus' (ancestor); 'atavismo'.

ex: Gli venne l'idea balzana di attraversare l'Atlantico a remi.
exEn: He had the harebrained idea of rowing across the Atlantic.
note: Originally of horses with white feet; 'idea balzana', 'cervello balzano'.

ex: Era un personaggio bislacco, sempre vestito di viola e circondato da gatti.
exEn: He was an oddball character, always dressed in purple and surrounded by cats.
note: Colloquial-literary; plural in -cchi/-cche.

ex: Nell'aria caliginosa della pianura i fari delle auto sembravano occhi di animali.
exEn: In the murky air of the plain the car headlights looked like animals' eyes.
note: Literary; noun 'caligine' (haze, smog). Figurative: 'una mente caliginosa'.

ex: Un'interpretazione cavillosa della norma ha bloccato l'intero progetto.
exEn: A hair-splitting interpretation of the rule blocked the whole project.
note: Pejorative; from 'cavillo'.

ex: Le armature corrusche dei cavalieri brillavano al sole del mattino.
exEn: The knights' glittering armour shone in the morning sun.
note: Rare, poetic (D'Annunzio); also 'corusco'.

ex: Il tempo edace ha cancellato le iscrizioni sulla facciata.
exEn: Devouring time has erased the inscriptions on the façade.
note: Poetic; from Ovid's 'tempus edax rerum'; almost only 'tempo edace'.

ex: L'efferato omicidio scosse la piccola comunità.
exEn: The brutal murder shook the small community.
note: Journalistic-literary; almost always 'efferato delitto/omicidio'; noun 'efferatezza'.

ex: Fu un crimine esecrabile che sollevò l'indignazione del paese.
exEn: It was an execrable crime that aroused the country's indignation.
note: Formal; verb 'esecrare', noun 'esecrazione'.

ex: La decisione di dividere l'esercito si rivelò esiziale.
exEn: The decision to split the army proved fatal.
note: Learned, from Latin 'exitium' (ruin); 'conseguenze esiziali'.

ex: Dal fondo del pozzo giungeva un lamento flebile.
exEn: From the bottom of the well came a faint moan.
note: Literary; mainly of sounds and voices; 'una flebile speranza'.

ex: Il vecchio giudice si alzò con gesto ieratico e impose il silenzio.
exEn: The old judge rose with a hieratic gesture and commanded silence.
note: From Greek 'hieros' (sacred); also of Byzantine art and hieratic script.

ex: Il declino dell'impero appariva ormai ineluttabile.
exEn: The empire's decline now appeared ineluctable.
note: Learned; 'destino ineluttabile'; noun 'ineluttabilità'.

ex: Il cammino verso l'accordo è irto di ostacoli.
exEn: The path towards an agreement is fraught with obstacles.
note: Literary; 'irto di' is the key collocation; also 'capelli irti' (bristly hair).

ex: I censori giudicarono lascive alcune scene del film.
exEn: The censors judged some scenes of the film lascivious.
note: Literary/formal; noun 'lascivia'.

ex: Nel bilancio c'era un errore madornale che nessuno aveva notato.
exEn: There was a glaring error in the budget that nobody had noticed.
note: Almost only 'errore/sbaglio madornale'.

ex: Con voce melliflua il venditore cercava di convincerla a firmare.
exEn: In a honeyed voice the salesman tried to persuade her to sign.
note: Usually pejorative in Italian (falsely sweet); literally 'flowing with honey'.

ex: Il tribunale ricostruì i nefandi delitti commessi nel campo.
exEn: The court reconstructed the heinous crimes committed in the camp.
note: Literary, from Latin 'nefandus' (not to be spoken); noun 'nefandezza'.

ex: L'atteggiamento ondivago del governo ha disorientato i mercati.
exEn: The government's wavering attitude disoriented the markets.
note: Journalistic-learned; from 'onda' + 'vagare'.

ex: Nonostante le smentite, il pervicace giornalista continuò a indagare.
exEn: Despite the denials, the stubborn journalist went on investigating.
note: Learned; can be admiring or critical; adverb 'pervicacemente'.

ex: La polemica sul regolamento era del tutto pretestuosa: il vero obiettivo era il presidente.
exEn: The row over the rules was entirely specious: the real target was the president.
note: From 'pretesto'; frequent in political and legal language ('ricorso pretestuoso').

ex: L'aggressione proditoria avvenne mentre la vittima dormiva.
exEn: The treacherous assault took place while the victim was asleep.
note: Legal-literary; from Latin 'proditor' (traitor). Adverb 'proditoriamente'.

ex: Era ritrosa a parlare di sé, ma generosa nell'ascoltare gli altri.
exEn: She was reluctant to talk about herself but generous in listening to others.
note: 'A ritroso' (backwards, in reverse) is the common fixed phrase; noun 'ritrosia'.

ex: Accolse la proposta con un sorriso sardonico.
exEn: He greeted the proposal with a sardonic smile.
note: From a Sardinian herb said to cause a grimacing laugh; 'riso sardonico'.

ex: La riforma era nata sbilenca e non ha retto alla prova dei fatti.
exEn: The reform was ill-conceived from the start and did not stand the test of reality.
note: Colloquial-expressive; 'un ragionamento sbilenco'.

ex: Fu abbastanza scaltro da non firmare nulla prima di consultare un legale.
exEn: He was shrewd enough not to sign anything before consulting a lawyer.
note: Neutral-to-admiring; noun 'scaltrezza'; cf. 'furbo' (colloquial, more negative).

ex: Il saggio abbonda di termini sesquipedali che oscurano un pensiero semplice.
exEn: The essay abounds in sesquipedalian terms that obscure a simple idea.
note: Learned/ironic, from Horace's 'sesquipedalia verba'; also 'errore sesquipedale' (huge).

ex: Il ministro ha risposto con una frase sibillina che ognuno ha interpretato a modo suo.
exEn: The minister replied with a sibylline sentence that everyone interpreted in their own way.
note: From the Sibyl's oracles; 'parole sibilline', 'sorriso sibillino'.

en: softly; in a low voice; humbly
ex: Mi permetto di osservare, sommessamente, che i dati dicono il contrario.
exEn: I venture to observe, with respect, that the data say the opposite.
note: Literary; in argument it is a polite hedge before a disagreement; adjective 'sommesso'.

ex: Con voce stentorea il banditore annunciò l'inizio dell'asta.
exEn: In a stentorian voice the auctioneer announced the start of the sale.
note: From Stentor in the Iliad; only of voices.

ex: La norma è stata introdotta surrettiziamente in un decreto su tutt'altra materia.
exEn: The provision was introduced surreptitiously into a decree on an entirely different subject.
note: Legal-learned; adjective 'surrettizio'.

ex: Rimase tetragono a ogni pressione e non cambiò il suo voto.
exEn: He remained unshakeable under every pressure and did not change his vote.
note: Literary, from Dante's 'ben tetragono ai colpi di ventura'; construction 'tetragono a'.

ex: Ci fissò con sguardo torvo e non disse una parola.
exEn: He stared at us with a grim look and did not say a word.
note: Literary; almost always 'sguardo/occhio torvo', 'guardare torvo'.

ex: Un uomo dall'aspetto truce sbarrava l'ingresso del locale.
exEn: A man of fierce appearance was blocking the entrance to the club.
note: Literary; 'sguardo truce', 'delitto truce'; adverb 'trucemente'.

ex: Le ubertose pianure del Po hanno nutrito per secoli le città del nord.
exEn: The fertile plains of the Po have fed the cities of the north for centuries.
note: Literary, from Latin 'uber' (abundant); 'campi ubertosi'.

ex: Gli schermi sono ormai ubiqui: in tasca, in auto, sui muri delle città.
exEn: Screens are now ubiquitous: in our pockets, in cars, on city walls.
note: Learned; noun 'ubiquità' ('avere il dono dell'ubiquità').

ex: Il discorso era elegante ma vacuo, privo di qualsiasi proposta concreta.
exEn: The speech was elegant but vacuous, devoid of any concrete proposal.
note: Learned; noun 'vacuità'. Cf. 'vuoto' (physical emptiness).

ex: Il vetusto palazzo aveva bisogno di un restauro urgente.
exEn: The ancient palace was in need of urgent restoration.
note: Literary/ironic; noun 'vetustà'.

ex: L'aggio del tabaccaio sui valori bollati è di pochi punti percentuali.
exEn: The tobacconist's commission on revenue stamps is a few percentage points.
note: Commercial/financial; 'aggio di emissione'. Opposite 'disaggio'. Not related to 'agio' (ease).

ex: I due finanzieri sono indagati per aggiotaggio dopo la diffusione di notizie false sul titolo.
exEn: The two financiers are under investigation for market rigging after false news about the stock was circulated.
note: Criminal-law term; from French 'agiotage'.

en: compounding of interest (charging interest on interest)
ex: La Cassazione ha dichiarato illegittimo l'anatocismo bancario trimestrale.
exEn: The Supreme Court declared quarterly bank compounding of interest unlawful.
note: Juridical/financial Greek-derived term; 'interessi anatocistici'.

ex: L'Italia ha mantenuto un avanzo primario per quasi tutti gli anni Duemila.
exEn: Italy maintained a primary surplus for almost all of the 2000s.
note: Public finance; opposite 'disavanzo primario'.

ex: La cartolarizzazione dei mutui subprime fu all'origine della crisi del 2008.
exEn: The securitisation of subprime mortgages was at the root of the 2008 crisis.
note: Financial jargon; from 'cartolare' (in paper form).

ex: La banca ha ridotto il castelletto dell'azienda da centomila a cinquantamila euro.
exEn: The bank cut the company's discount facility from one hundred thousand to fifty thousand euros.
note: Banking jargon; literally 'little castle'. Cf. 'fido' (general credit line).

ex: L'immobile è iscritto a bilancio tra i cespiti ammortizzabili.
exEn: The building is entered in the accounts among the depreciable assets.
note: Accounting/legal; from Latin 'caespes' (turf). 'Registro dei cespiti' = fixed-asset register.

ex: I creditori chirografari vengono soddisfatti solo dopo quelli privilegiati.
exEn: Unsecured creditors are paid only after the secured ones.
note: Bankruptcy law; from Greek 'cheirographon' (handwritten document). Opposite 'privilegiato', 'ipotecario'.

ex: La società ha chiesto il concordato preventivo per evitare il fallimento.
exEn: The company applied for a composition with creditors to avoid bankruptcy.
note: Insolvency-law procedure; compare 'liquidazione giudiziale'.

ex: «Resilienza» è una parola di nuovo conio entrata ovunque.
exEn: 'Resilience' is a newly coined word that has got in everywhere.
note: Literal (die for minting) and figurative: 'di nuovo conio' (newly coined), 'dello stesso conio' (of the same ilk).

en: quota system; rationing of imports or supplies
ex: Il contingentamento delle importazioni di acciaio ha scatenato una guerra commerciale.
exEn: The quota system on steel imports triggered a trade war.
note: Trade-policy term, from 'contingente' (quota); verb 'contingentare'.

ex: Nel 1866 il governo decretò il corso forzoso della lira, sospendendo la convertibilità in oro.
exEn: In 1866 the government decreed forced currency for the lira, suspending gold convertibility.
note: Monetary history; cf. 'corso legale' (legal tender).

en: receivership; trusteeship (in bankruptcy or guardianship); editorship
ex: La curatela fallimentare ha messo all'asta i macchinari dell'azienda.
exEn: The bankruptcy receivership put the company's machinery up for auction.
note: The 'curatore fallimentare' is the receiver; in publishing 'a cura di' = edited by.

ex: Il Comune ha dichiarato il dissesto finanziario e non può più pagare i fornitori.
exEn: The municipality declared financial collapse and can no longer pay its suppliers.
note: Also 'dissesto idrogeologico' (landslide and flood risk).

ex: L'Unione ha accusato alcuni produttori stranieri di dumping sull'acciaio.
exEn: The Union accused some foreign producers of dumping steel.
note: English loan, invariable; also 'dumping sociale/fiscale'.

en: emphyteusis (long lease of land with duty to improve)
ex: Il terreno era gravato da un'enfiteusi risalente al Settecento.
exEn: The land was encumbered by an emphyteutic lease dating back to the eighteenth century.
note: Juridical (Civil Code, art. 957 ff.); the holder is the 'enfiteuta', the owner the 'concedente'. Invariable.

en: enforcement (of a guarantee); examination (of a witness)
ex: La banca ha proceduto all'escussione della fideiussione dopo il mancato pagamento.
exEn: The bank proceeded to enforce the guarantee after the payment default.
note: Verb 'escutere'; 'beneficio di escussione' (guarantor's right to have the debtor pursued first).

en: fictitious foreign residence (of a company, to evade tax)
ex: La Guardia di Finanza contesta al gruppo un'esterovestizione durata dieci anni.
exEn: The tax police accuse the group of a ten-year fictitious foreign residence.
note: Tax-law neologism ('vestire da estero'); typical of financial journalism.

ex: Le filande della Brianza impiegavano soprattutto donne e bambine.
exEn: The silk mills of Brianza employed mainly women and girls.
note: Economic and social history of Northern Italy; the worker was a 'filandera' (regional).

ex: Nei racconti popolari il gabelliere è sempre avido e odiato.
exEn: In folk tales the tax collector is always greedy and hated.
note: From 'gabella' (duty); today only historical or contemptuous. Cf. 'esattore' (neutral).

en: endorsement (of a cheque or bill); turn, stroll
ex: L'assegno non trasferibile non può circolare mediante girata.
exEn: A non-transferable cheque cannot circulate by endorsement.
note: Financial sense; 'girante' (endorser), 'giratario'.

ex: Gli incagli sono cresciuti più delle sofferenze nel bilancio della banca.
exEn: Unlikely-to-pay loans grew faster than bad loans in the bank's accounts.
note: Banking classification ('crediti incagliati', between 'in bonis' and 'in sofferenza'); nautical sense = grounding.

ex: Prima dell'annuncio qualcuno aveva fatto incetta di azioni della società.
exEn: Before the announcement someone had bought up shares in the company.
note: Fixed collocation 'fare incetta di'; can be neutral or imply speculation.

ex: Il commercialista ha ricostruito i movimenti sospetti dal libro mastro.
exEn: The accountant reconstructed the suspicious transactions from the general ledger.
note: Accounting; often just 'il mastro'. Cf. 'libro giornale' (journal), 'prima nota' (daybook).

ex: L'ex tesoriere è accusato di malversazione ai danni del partito.
exEn: The former treasurer is accused of embezzling party funds.
note: Legal term; 'malversazione a danno dello Stato'.

ex: Le minusvalenze possono essere compensate con le plusvalenze dei quattro anni successivi.
exEn: Capital losses can be offset against capital gains over the following four years.
note: Tax and accounting jargon.

ex: Nel mercato dei braccianti stagionali la grande distribuzione agisce quasi come un monopsonio.
exEn: In the seasonal farm-labour market, large retailers act almost as a monopsony.
note: Economics; mirror image of 'monopolio'. Adjective 'monopsonistico'.

ex: Le parti hanno convenuto una novazione del contratto originario.
exEn: The parties agreed on a novation of the original contract.
note: Strictly juridical (art. 1230 c.c.); do not confuse with 'innovazione'.

ex: L'antico opificio tessile è diventato un museo di archeologia industriale.
exEn: The old textile works has become a museum of industrial archaeology.
note: Formal/dated ('Opificio delle Pietre Dure' in Florence); neutral 'fabbrica', 'stabilimento'.

ex: Firmò un pagherò a novanta giorni per saldare la fornitura.
exEn: He signed a ninety-day promissory note to settle the supply.
note: Commercial law ('pagherò cambiario'); invariable, from 'io pagherò'. Cf. 'cambiale', 'tratta'.

ex: La partita doppia fu codificata da Luca Pacioli nel 1494.
exEn: Double-entry bookkeeping was codified by Luca Pacioli in 1494.
note: Accounting; 'tenere la contabilità in partita doppia'.

ex: I tre soci fondatori hanno stretto un patto parasociale sul diritto di voto.
exEn: The three founding partners entered into a shareholders' agreement on voting rights.
note: Company law (art. 2341-bis c.c.); binds the parties but not the company itself.

en: pledge; pawn; security (on movable property); token
ex: Per ottenere il prestito ha dato in pegno i gioielli di famiglia.
exEn: To obtain the loan she pledged the family jewels.
note: 'Monte di pietà/monte dei pegni' (pawnshop); figurative 'in pegno d'amicizia'.

en: pre-emption right; right of first refusal
ex: L'inquilino ha esercitato il diritto di prelazione e ha acquistato l'appartamento.
exEn: The tenant exercised his right of first refusal and bought the flat.
note: Fixed phrase 'diritto di prelazione'.

ex: Le spese straordinarie si ripartiscono pro quota tra i condòmini.
exEn: Extraordinary expenses are divided among the co-owners in proportion to their shares.
note: Latinism, legal/administrative register; cf. 'pro rata' (by time), 'pro capite' (per head).

en: pro rata; in proportion to time or share
ex: Gli interessi maturano pro rata temporis, giorno per giorno.
exEn: Interest accrues pro rata temporis, day by day.
note: Latinism of law and accounting; often with 'temporis'. Adjective/noun 'pro rata' also in 'il prorata IVA'.

en: protest (formal declaration of non-payment of a bill or cheque)
ex: Dopo il protesto dell'assegno il suo nome è finito nel registro dei cattivi pagatori.
exEn: After the cheque was protested his name ended up on the register of bad payers.
note: Not 'protesta'; 'protestato' = someone with a protested bill.

ex: I ratei attivi rappresentano ricavi di competenza dell'esercizio non ancora incassati.
exEn: Accrued income represents revenue for the period not yet collected.
note: Accounting jargon; paired with 'risconto' (deferral).

en: voluntary correction of a tax return with reduced penalties
ex: Ha regolarizzato la posizione con il ravvedimento operoso, pagando una sanzione ridotta.
exEn: He regularised his position through voluntary correction, paying a reduced penalty.
note: Italian tax-law institution; 'ravvedimento' alone is literary for 'repentance'.

ex: La vedova percepisce la pensione di reversibilità del marito.
exEn: The widow receives her husband's survivor's pension.
note: Welfare law ('pensione di reversibilità'); in science 'reversibilità di una reazione'.

ex: Il referendum del 1985 abrogò il meccanismo della scala mobile.
exEn: The 1985 referendum abolished the wage-indexation mechanism.
note: In economic history the automatic link between wages and inflation (1945-1992); the everyday meaning is 'escalator'.

en: shell company in a chain of holdings; Chinese box
ex: Il gruppo controllava la fabbrica attraverso una catena di scatole cinesi.
exEn: The group controlled the factory through a chain of nested holding companies.
note: Financial-journalism metaphor for pyramidal holdings; literally nested boxes.

ex: Il signoraggio della banca centrale è un tema caro ai teorici del complotto.
exEn: Central-bank seigniorage is a favourite topic of conspiracy theorists.
note: Monetary economics; historically the lord's right to mint coins.

ex: La stagflazione degli anni Settanta mise in crisi le ricette keynesiane.
exEn: The stagflation of the 1970s put Keynesian recipes in crisis.
note: Blend of 'stagnazione' and 'inflazione'.

ex: La catena dei subappalti rende difficile controllare la sicurezza nei cantieri.
exEn: The chain of subcontracts makes it hard to monitor safety on building sites.
note: 'Subappaltatore'; 'appalto' = contract awarded by tender.

ex: Con la surroga abbiamo trasferito il mutuo a una banca con un tasso migliore.
exEn: Through a subrogation we transferred the mortgage to a bank with a better rate.
note: Banking/legal; also 'surrogazione'. In politics 'surroga' is the replacement of a resigned member.

en: life annuity; lifetime pension (esp. of former MPs)
ex: Il taglio dei vitalizi degli ex parlamentari è stato al centro di un lungo dibattito.
exEn: The cut to former MPs' lifetime pensions was at the centre of a long debate.
note: Also adjective: 'rendita vitalizia', 'senatore a vita'.

ex: Dopo il lutto cadde in un'abulia da cui nemmeno il lavoro riusciva a scuoterlo.
exEn: After the bereavement he sank into an abulia from which not even work could rouse him.
note: Psychological/literary (Greek); adjective 'abulico'. Stronger and more clinical than 'apatia'; 'accidia' is the moral-theological sloth.

ex: L'accidia, per i teologi medievali, era il torpore dell'anima che rifiuta il bene.
exEn: For medieval theologians, acedia was the torpor of the soul that refuses the good.
note: One of the seven deadly sins; today literary for 'listless indolence'. Adjective: accidioso. Dante punishes the slothful in the Stygian marsh.

ex: Rispose con un'acredine che tradiva anni di rancore mai espresso.
exEn: She answered with an acrimony that betrayed years of never-voiced resentment.
note: Literary; the literal sense is the sharpness of a taste. Synonyms: acrimonia, asprezza, astio. Adjective: acre.

ex: Nelle sue ultime poesie si avverte un afflato religioso del tutto nuovo.
exEn: In his last poems one senses an entirely new religious inspiration.
note: Elevated (aulico; Latin afflatus, 'breath'). Collocations: 'afflato lirico/poetico/mistico/umanitario'.

ex: Attese il verdetto in preda a un'ambascia che le impediva di respirare.
exEn: She awaited the verdict in the grip of an anguish that stopped her breathing.
note: Literary; originally physical breathlessness (Dante), later moral anguish. Synonyms: angoscia, affanno, angustia.

ex: Vivevano nelle angustie, ma non lo lasciarono mai trapelare agli amici.
exEn: They lived in straitened circumstances, but never let it show to their friends.
note: Literary; in the plural often 'financial straits'. Verb: angustiarsi (to worry). Compare the look-alike adjective 'angusto' (narrow).

ex: L'assillo del denaro lo accompagnò per tutta la vita.
exEn: The nagging worry about money accompanied him all his life.
note: In its literal sense 'assillo' is the gadfly. Verb: assillare (to pester relentlessly); adjective: assillante.

ex: Un vecchio professore atrabiliare bocciava metà della classe per principio.
exEn: A morose old professor failed half the class on principle.
note: Literary/jocular; from the 'black bile' of ancient medicine (the humour of melancholy). Synonyms: bilioso, ipocondriaco (archaic sense), scontroso.

ex: Parlava dei suoi successi con una boria che allontanava anche gli amici.
exEn: He spoke of his successes with a conceit that drove away even his friends.
note: Pejorative. Adjective: borioso. Close to 'iattanza' (literary) and 'spocchia' (colloquial).

ex: Guardava le vetrine con la bramosia di chi non ha mai potuto comprare nulla.
exEn: He looked at the shop windows with the craving of someone who has never been able to buy anything.
note: Literary, from 'bramare'. Synonyms: brama (shorter form), cupidigia (pejorative), avidità. Adjective: bramoso.

ex: I moralisti del Seicento vedevano nella concupiscenza la radice di ogni peccato.
exEn: Seventeenth-century moralists saw concupiscence as the root of every sin.
note: Theological/literary; now often ironic. Near-synonyms by register: 'libidine', 'lussuria' (sin), 'bramosia' (greedy longing).

ex: La notizia del fallimento gettò i dipendenti nella costernazione.
exEn: The news of the bankruptcy threw the employees into consternation.
note: Formal/literary. Adjective: costernato. Stronger than 'sgomento', weaker than 'disperazione'.

ex: Il suo unico cruccio era di non aver mai fatto pace con il fratello.
exEn: His one nagging sorrow was never having made peace with his brother.
note: Literary/formal. 'Darsi cruccio' = to fret; adjective crucciato ('viso crucciato' = a troubled, frowning face, like corrucciato, accigliato).

ex: Il giudice ascoltò entrambe le parti con la stessa equanimità.
exEn: The judge listened to both sides with the same equanimity.
note: Formal; in Italian it stresses impartiality as much as calm. Adjective 'equanime'. Cf. 'imperturbabilità' (unflappability), 'atarassia' (philosophical).

en: outburst of rage; fit of temper
ex: Al terzo errore del cameriere il cliente diede in escandescenze.
exEn: At the waiter's third mistake the customer flew into a rage.
note: Almost exclusively in the idiom 'dare in escandescenze'. Synonyms: andare su tutte le furie, perdere le staffe.

ex: Le campane suonarono a giubilo per la fine della guerra.
exEn: The bells rang out in jubilation for the end of the war.
note: Literary/solemn. Not to be confused with 'giubileo' (jubilee, holy year). Verb: giubilare; 'suonare a giubilo'.

ex: Entrò giulivo nella stanza, ignaro del disastro che lo aspettava.
exEn: He walked blithely into the room, unaware of the disaster awaiting him.
note: Literary, today mostly ironic ('tutto giulivo'); 'giulivo' suggests naive, slightly foolish cheer. Neutral 'allegro', 'lieto'.

ex: Il vecchio, iracondo e sordo, urlava contro chiunque entrasse nel cortile.
exEn: The old man, wrathful and deaf, shouted at anyone who came into the yard.
note: Literary Latinism; noun 'iracondia'. Dante's 'iracondi' in Inferno VII. Neutral 'irascibile', 'collerico'.

ex: L'irresolutezza del comandante costò alla flotta la giornata.
exEn: The commander's irresoluteness cost the fleet the day.
note: Formal/literary; adjective 'irresoluto'. Cf. 'indecisione' (neutral), 'titubanza', 'tentennamento' (wavering).

ex: Un dolce languore la prese al pensiero dell'estate ormai lontana.
exEn: A sweet languor came over her at the thought of the now distant summer.
note: Literary; also physical: 'un languore allo stomaco' (a feeling of hunger). Adjective: languido; verb: languire.

ex: Una letizia pacata illuminava il volto del vecchio frate.
exEn: A quiet gladness lit up the old friar's face.
note: Elevated (aulico)/religious (Latin laetitia). Adjective: lieto (more common). Synonyms: gioia (neutral), gaudio (solemn), allegrezza (literary).

ex: Sopportò le offese del fratello con una longanimità che rasentava la santità.
exEn: He bore his brother's insults with a forbearance that bordered on sainthood.
note: Literary/religious Latinism (longanimitas); adjective 'longanime'. Neutral 'pazienza', 'tolleranza'.

en: lump in the throat; heavy heart; pang of sadness
ex: Alla stazione le venne il magone e non riuscì a dire nemmeno 'ciao'.
exEn: At the station she got a lump in her throat and could not even say goodbye.
note: Northern regional (Lombard 'magón', literally 'stomach'), now widespread in familiar speech. 'Avere il magone', 'far venire il magone'.

ex: Con aria mesta ripiegò la lettera e la ripose nel cassetto.
exEn: With a wistful air he folded the letter and put it back in the drawer.
note: Literary; denotes a composed, quiet sadness. Noun: mestizia. Synonyms: malinconico, afflitto.

ex: La sua ombrosità rendeva difficile fargli qualsiasi osservazione.
exEn: His touchiness made it hard to make any remark to him at all.
note: Formal; adjective 'ombroso', originally of a horse that shies at shadows. Cf. 'permalosità' (quick to take offence), 'suscettibilità'.

ex: Preferì l'esilio all'onta di una condanna pubblica.
exEn: He preferred exile to the disgrace of a public conviction.
note: Literary. 'A onta di' = despite (archaic). Synonyms: vergogna (common), disonore, ignominia, obbrobrio.

ex: Con il figlio in viaggio ogni telefonata mancata era un patema.
exEn: With her son travelling, every missed phone call was a source of anxiety.
note: Almost only in 'patema d'animo'. Masculine noun in -a (like 'problema'). Formal or ironic in tone.

ex: Con voce querula si lamentava del freddo, del cibo e dei vicini.
exEn: In a querulous voice he complained about the cold, the food and the neighbours.
note: Literary (Latin querulus). Of a voice, tone or person. Synonyms: lamentoso, piagnucoloso (familiar).

ex: Il rovello di non sapere chi l'avesse tradito lo tenne sveglio per notti intere.
exEn: The torment of not knowing who had betrayed him kept him awake for whole nights.
note: Literary (from 'rovellarsi', 'arrovellarsi'). Synonyms: assillo, tormento, cruccio.

ex: La notizia del licenziamento fu accolta con sbigottimento generale.
exEn: The news of the dismissal was received with general dismay.
note: Formal; adjective 'sbigottito', verb 'sbigottire'. Near-synonyms: 'sgomento' (dread-tinged), 'costernazione' (grief), 'stupore' (surprise).

ex: Dopo il terzo rifiuto fu preso da uno scoramento che gli fece abbandonare il progetto.
exEn: After the third rejection he was seized by a despondency that made him abandon the project.
note: Literary/formal; from 'scorarsi'. Synonyms on a scale: delusione < sconforto < scoramento < avvilimento < prostrazione.

ex: Con grande scorno dei rivali, la squadra di provincia vinse il torneo.
exEn: To the great mortification of their rivals, the provincial team won the tournament.
note: Literary; 'con scorno di', 'a scorno di' (in defiance of). Adjective: scornato (disappointed and humiliated).

en: humiliating setback; snub; blow to one's pride
ex: Perdere in casa contro l'ultima in classifica fu uno smacco difficile da digerire.
exEn: Losing at home to the bottom team was a humiliating setback that was hard to swallow.
note: Journalistic in tone; 'subire uno smacco', 'che smacco!'. More concrete than 'umiliazione'.

ex: Rispose con sussiego, senza degnarsi di guardare l'interlocutore.
exEn: He answered with stiff hauteur, without deigning to look at the person addressing him.
note: Literary; from Spanish 'sosiego'. Adjective: sussiegoso. Denotes an ostentatious, aloof gravity.

ex: Il tedio delle domeniche di provincia lo spinse a partire per la capitale.
exEn: The tedium of provincial Sundays drove him to leave for the capital.
note: Literary; Leopardi uses it for existential boredom. Adjective: tedioso; verb: tediare (to bore).

ex: La tetraggine di quelle stanze chiuse gli opprimeva l'animo.
exEn: The gloominess of those shuttered rooms weighed on his spirit.
note: From 'tetro'. Literary; used of both places and moods. Synonyms: cupezza, lugubrità.

ex: Recitò la parte con un trasporto che commosse persino i critici più freddi.
exEn: He played the part with a fervour that moved even the coldest critics.
note: Emotional sense, distinct from the concrete one ('trasporto merci'). 'Con trasporto' = with passionate enthusiasm. Synonyms: slancio, foga, ardore.

en: exultation; riot (of colour, joy); jubilant celebration
ex: Il gol allo scadere scatenò un tripudio di bandiere e cori sugli spalti.
exEn: The last-minute goal set off a riot of flags and chants in the stands.
note: Literary/journalistic; also figurative: 'un tripudio di colori/sapori'. Verb: tripudiare.

ex: Il sindaco, tronfio per la vittoria, non ringraziò nessuno dei suoi collaboratori.
exEn: The mayor, puffed up with victory, thanked none of his staff.
note: Pejorative/literary; also of style ('prosa tronfia' = bombastic). Synonyms: borioso, pettoruto, gonfio.

ex: Quella pioggia sottile e continua gli metteva un'uggia addosso che non passava.
exEn: That thin, continuous rain gave him a gloom that would not lift.
note: Tuscan/literary. 'Avere in uggia qualcuno' = to be unable to stand someone; 'venire a uggia' = to become tiresome. Adjective: uggioso ('tempo uggioso' = dreary weather).

en: at some indefinite future date; never (of payment)
ex: Mi ha promesso di restituirmi i soldi, ma a babbo morto.
exEn: He promised to pay me back, but heaven knows when.
note: Tuscan colloquialism (literally 'when Dad dies', i.e. on inheritance); 'pagare a babbo morto'.

en: a fortiori; all the more so
ex: Se la regola vale per i dipendenti, a fortiori vale per i dirigenti.
exEn: If the rule applies to employees, a fortiori it applies to managers.
note: Latin; logical and legal argumentation. Italian equivalent: 'a maggior ragione'.

en: at other people's expense; without paying
ex: Si è presentato alla festa senza invito e ha mangiato a ufo tutta la sera.
exEn: He turned up at the party uninvited and ate for free all evening.
note: Colloquial ('mangiare/vivere a ufo'); folk etymology from 'ad usum fabricae' stamped on duty-free goods.

en: ad hoc; made or chosen for a specific purpose
ex: Il governo ha istituito una commissione ad hoc per esaminare il caso.
exEn: The government set up an ad hoc commission to examine the case.
note: Latin; also pejorative: 'una spiegazione ad hoc' (a convenient rationalisation).

ex: Complimenti per la laurea: ad maiora!
exEn: Congratulations on your degree: on to greater things!
note: Latin toast/wish, sometimes 'ad maiora semper'; academic and formal-friendly register.

en: kingmaker; decisive factor (holder of the balance of power)
ex: Con i suoi pochi seggi il piccolo partito è diventato l'ago della bilancia.
exEn: With its few seats the small party has become the kingmaker.
note: Literally the needle of the scales; political commentary.

ex: Ho inviato le dimissioni: alea iacta est.
exEn: I've sent in my resignation: the die is cast.
note: Caesar at the Rubicon; Italian equivalent 'il dado è tratto'.

ex: Ha fatto i compiti alla carlona, tanto per finire.
exEn: He did his homework any old how, just to get it done.
note: Colloquial; from 'Carlone', the bluff Charlemagne of chivalric poems. Cf. 'alla buona', 'alla bell'e meglio'.

en: to eat humble pie; to make a humiliating climb-down
ex: Dopo lo strappo, il segretario è dovuto andare a Canossa dagli alleati.
exEn: After the rift, the party secretary had to go cap in hand to his allies.
note: From Henry IV's penance before Gregory VII at Canossa (1077); political journalism.

ex: La trasparenza totale è un'arma a doppio taglio: informa i cittadini ma espone i testimoni.
exEn: Total transparency is a double-edged sword: it informs citizens but exposes witnesses.
note: 'Essere un'arma a doppio taglio'.

en: and that's the end of that; nothing more to be done
ex: Se il giudice accetta il ricorso, buonanotte al secchio: si ricomincia da capo.
exEn: If the judge accepts the appeal, that's that: we start all over again.
note: Colloquial, resigned; alludes to a bucket dropped in the well. Also 'buonanotte suonatori'.

en: you'll be waiting a long time; don't hold your breath
ex: Aspettare il rimborso dallo Stato? Campa cavallo che l'erba cresce.
exEn: Waiting for a refund from the State? Don't hold your breath.
note: Proverb ('live on, horse, the grass is growing'); often just 'campa cavallo!'.

ex: Quella sinfonia fu il canto del cigno del compositore, morto pochi mesi dopo.
exEn: That symphony was the composer's swan song; he died a few months later.
note: From the legend that swans sing before dying.

ex: Il ministro ha dovuto ammettere l'errore coram populo.
exEn: The minister had to admit the mistake in public.
note: Latinism; often ironic. Cf. 'pubblicamente', 'alla luce del sole'.

en: with a grain of salt; with discernment
ex: Le statistiche vanno lette cum grano salis, tenendo conto di come sono state raccolte.
exEn: Statistics must be read with a grain of salt, bearing in mind how they were collected.
note: Latin (Pliny); learned register.

ex: Di riffa o di raffa è riuscito a farsi assumere in Comune.
exEn: By hook or by crook he managed to get hired by the town council.
note: Colloquial ('riffa' = force/raffle, 'raffa' = grab); syn. 'in un modo o nell'altro'.

en: tit-for-tat exchange; you scratch my back
ex: La politica delle nomine era un puro do ut des.
exEn: The appointments policy was pure horse-trading.
note: Latin 'I give so that you give'; this, not 'quid pro quo', renders the English 'quid pro quo'.

ex: Il relatore cominciò ex abrupto, senza saluti né premesse.
exEn: The speaker began abruptly, with no greetings or preamble.
note: Latinism, rhetorical/formal; also 'di punto in bianco' (colloquial).

ex: Non tollerava che si parlasse ex cathedra di argomenti che non si conoscevano.
exEn: He couldn't stand people pronouncing with authority on subjects they didn't know.
note: From papal infallibility ('parlare ex cathedra'); today usually ironic about pompous pronouncements.

ex: Dopo l'incendio l'archivio è stato ricostruito ex novo.
exEn: After the fire the archive was rebuilt from scratch.
note: Latin; 'ricominciare ex novo'.

en: an unrequested excuse is an obvious self-accusation
ex: Nessuno ti aveva accusato: excusatio non petita, accusatio manifesta.
exEn: Nobody had accused you: an unprompted excuse is a manifest confession.
note: Medieval Latin maxim, often shortened to 'excusatio non petita'; learned, ironic.

ex: Il licenziamento dev'essere l'extrema ratio, non la prima risposta.
exEn: Dismissal must be the last resort, not the first response.
note: Latinism, juridical and formal; 'ricorrere all'extrema ratio'. Neutral 'ultima spiaggia' (colloquial).

en: to sneak in without paying; to fare-dodge
ex: Ha fatto il portoghese sull'autobus per anni prima di essere multato.
exEn: He dodged the bus fare for years before getting fined.
note: Colloquial; from an 18th-century Roman anecdote about a free show for the Portuguese embassy. Not offensive to Portuguese people in intent, but best explained.

en: the sting is in the tail
ex: La recensione era elogiosa, ma in cauda venenum: l'ultima riga la stroncava.
exEn: The review was full of praise, but the sting was in the tail: the last line panned it.
note: Latin ('poison in the tail', of the scorpion); used of speeches or letters ending with a barb.

en: at the last moment; in extremis
ex: L'accordo è stato raggiunto in extremis, poche ore prima della scadenza.
exEn: The agreement was reached at the last moment, a few hours before the deadline.
note: Latin; originally 'on the point of death'.

en: in the making; in progress, not yet complete
ex: Il progetto è ancora in fieri e potrebbe cambiare radicalmente.
exEn: The project is still in the making and could change radically.
note: Latin; learned.

en: along the way; during the process
ex: La valutazione in itinere permette di correggere il corso prima della fine.
exEn: Ongoing assessment makes it possible to correct the course before the end.
note: Latin; education and administration jargon; also 'infortunio in itinere' (commuting accident).

en: 'he himself said it'; appeal to authority
ex: Non basta un ipse dixit del direttore per chiudere la discussione.
exEn: A mere 'because the director says so' is not enough to close the discussion.
note: Latin, from the Pythagoreans' reverence for their master; used as a noun ('un ipse dixit').

en: Procrustean bed (forcing things into a rigid scheme)
ex: Ridurre ogni cultura a un unico modello è un letto di Procuste.
exEn: Reducing every culture to a single model is a Procrustean bed.
note: Mythological allusion, learned/essayistic register.

en: with the necessary changes; all due allowances made
ex: Il ragionamento vale, mutatis mutandis, anche per le piccole imprese.
exEn: The argument holds, mutatis mutandis, for small businesses too.
note: Latin; typical of legal and academic prose.

ex: La questione dei confini resta il nodo gordiano del negoziato.
exEn: The border question remains the Gordian knot of the negotiation.
note: Classical allusion; 'tagliare il nodo gordiano' = to solve drastically.

en: willy-nilly; whether one likes it or not
ex: Nolens volens, dovremo adeguarci alle nuove regole europee.
exEn: Like it or not, we shall have to comply with the new European rules.
note: Latin; Italian equivalent 'volente o nolente'.

ex: Ha accettato il compromesso obtorto collo, dopo giorni di resistenza.
exEn: He accepted the compromise reluctantly, after days of resistance.
note: Latin ('with twisted neck'); learned register.

ex: Orsù, non perdiamoci in chiacchiere e cominciamo.
exEn: Come now, let's not waste time chatting and get started.
note: Archaic/literary, now jocular; cf. 'suvvia', 'dai' (colloquial).

en: ball and chain; dead weight, hindrance
ex: Il debito pubblico è una palla al piede per la crescita del paese.
exEn: The public debt is a ball and chain on the country's growth.
note: Usually 'essere/avere una palla al piede'.

en: misunderstanding; taking one thing for another
ex: C'è stato un qui pro quo: credevano che la riunione fosse domani.
exEn: There was a mix-up: they thought the meeting was tomorrow.
note: FALSE FRIEND: in Italian it means a misunderstanding (also written 'quiproquo' or, less commonly, 'quid pro quo'), never an exchange of favours, which is 'do ut des'.

en: without a fight; without striking a blow
ex: L'esercito entrò nella città senza colpo ferire.
exEn: The army entered the city without striking a blow.
note: Literary/journalistic, with an archaic word order (object before infinitive).

ex: La minaccia di licenziamento pendeva su di lui come una spada di Damocle.
exEn: The threat of dismissal hung over him like a sword of Damocles.
note: Classical allusion; 'avere una spada di Damocle sulla testa'.

en: sui generis; of its own kind; unusual
ex: È un contratto sui generis che non rientra in nessuna delle categorie previste dal codice.
exEn: It is a sui generis contract that fits none of the categories provided for by the code.
